hardware_answers.question: Does a board on the sibling's 1.2.0 web-flasher image sync and capture Wi-Fi, zigbee and btle under both final helpers? What are the BTLE fix-up behaviour and message text, and the length checks (no false drops)?

answers.answer: Yes, on the Kismet side (the extcap part, id 130, was not run). Board D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image synced and captured all three radios under the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers. Wi-Fi: 792 / 516 / 342 packets. Zigbee: 200/200 TXTEST frames each, link type 230. BTLE: 2536 / 1141 / 633 packets, with 13/12/12 devices. The board sends flags 0x0013 and a zero CRC. Every helper rewrites each record to 0x0C13 with a valid CRC (100% of 4,323 pcapng packets checked) and logs this once per helper connection, verbatim: '<name>: the board's firmware does not mark BTLE packets as CRC checked, so Kismet would drop them; the helper fills in the CRC and the flags (the board only reports packets whose CRC passed). Flashing current firmware makes this unnecessary'. In Kismet it reads 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a local source and 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a remote one. There were 0 'impossible length' drops and 0 error packets. The only differences from current firmware are the fix-up message and the 0x0013 flags on the wire.
answers.evidence: f10w.out, f10z.out, f10b.out, f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10raw.json

answers.answer: Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_answers.question: What do common serial terminals (screen, minicom, picocom, pyserial's miniterm; idf.py monitor if present) do to DTR/RTS on these boards? Do they take the flock the helpers check? What happens to a capture when one has the port open, and the reverse?

answers.answer:
Four terminals were tried; none reset an idle board (no ROM boot text within 5 s).

- pyserial miniterm: flock, no TIOCEXCL, raises DTR and RTS.
- picocom 3.1: flock, no TIOCEXCL, no modem-line writes.
- screen 4.9.1: TIOCEXCL, no flock, TIOCMSET DTR|RTS|CTS.
- minicom 2.10: neither flock nor TIOCEXCL, only a UUCP lock file /var/lock/LCK..ttyACM2. TIOCMSET DTR|RTS|CTS at open and [0] at exit.

With a helper holding the board, all four are refused. With picocom, miniterm or screen holding it, the Python helper and a C local source are refused with 'already in use'. With minicom holding it, both helpers open the board anyway and capture breaks. screen also leaves a detached SCREEN process holding the port after its client is killed.
answers.evidence:
Messages with the Python helper holding (p21/p21b/p21c):
- miniterm: "could not open port '/dev/ttyACM2': [Errno 16] ... Device or resource busy".
- picocom: 'FATAL: cannot open /dev/ttyACM2: Device or resource busy'.
- minicom: exit 1, prints nothing.
- screen: "Cannot open line '/dev/ttyACM2' for R/W: Device or resource busy".

With minicom holding:
- Python helper: '/dev/ttyACM2 opened' then '/dev/ttyACM2: device reports readiness to read but returned no data (device disconnected or multiple access on port?)'. No packets.
- C local btle source: opened the board and rebooted it into BLE; minicom saw 4 boot texts.

The terminals were extracted from apt-get download .debs into ~/e2e/term; no sudo. idf.py monitor is not on the Pi. The board was set back to Wi-Fi afterwards.

hardware_answers.question: BLE on the air: is BLE 5 extended advertising not captured? Is SCAN_RSP never captured (passive scan), so names sent only in scan responses are missing? What scan duty cycle does the controller really give?

answers.answer: Passive parts settled; the active parts (own adverts from hci0) could not be run. (1) Extended advertising: none is captured. The firmware uses the legacy NimBLE passive scan and drops any report with more than 31 data bytes (sniff_ble: data_len > 31 -> s_oversize++). In 12,695 records from 6 captures, the only PDU types were ADV_IND (0) and ADV_NONCONN_IND (2), and the longest AdvData was 31 bytes (2217 of 3644 records at exactly 31). No extended advertiser nearby was known, so absence on air is shown but not proven against a known source. (2) SCAN_RSP: 0 in 12,695 records (PDU type 4 never seen), and no ADV_SCAN_IND or ADV_DIRECT_IND either. So a device that names itself only in a scan response will appear without a name (inferred, not shown with a known device). The wiki's 'scan responses are rare' is effectively 'never'. (3) Duty cycle: the scan listens almost continuously. The strongest regular advertiser (0e:0a:43:01:2a:dd, -34 dBm, 100 ms interval, median gap 105.0 ms, minimum 98.9 ms) was heard 1119 times in 120 s against 28 missed events: 97.6% of its advertising events. The largest gap in the whole stream was 197 ms. Weaker advertisers were heard less often (61-81%), limited by signal. (4) The Pi's own hci0 cannot be used without sudo: 'PowerState: off-blocked' (rfkill soft block) and /dev/rfkill is root:root 0664. So there was no own advertising at a known interval, no extended-advert test and no active-scan name comparison.
answers.evidence: hw2/results-ble-oldfw/b9raw.json, b9raw.out, b9k.an, f10raw.json; firmware/main/esp32c5_sniffer.c:542-550, 1175-1183; bluetoothctl show; ls -la /dev/rfkill

hardware_answers.question: What are the Python remote helper's handshake timings (0.8 s settle, 2 s first open, 6 s no-answer reopen, 15 s give-up) and exact message texts, including the normal connected/opening/opened/capturing lines and the Troubleshooting table texts?

answers.answer: C local part only: a silent port gives 'silent: no answer, reconnecting' at about 6 s, and at 15 s the helper exits. Kismet shows only 'IPC connection closed'; the helper's text '<name>: no capture from the board on <dev> for 15 seconds; is it flashed with the esp32c5 sniffer firmware, and is nothing else holding the port?' is written to the IPC but never shown. Kismet re-opens 5 s later. The MODE->START gap in strace is 0.80-0.83 s.
answers.evidence: n15.log and strace, n1.log, strace 168599/168648 (MODE at 31.990 -> START 32.792).

answers.answer:
Python handshake on a silent board (ROM download mode via esptool --after no-reset chip-id), timed from 'opened':
- MODE WIFI at +0.10 s, START at +0.90 s, MODE again every 2.0 s.
- 'INFO: /dev/ttyACM2: no answer for 6 s, reopening' at +6.03 s. Later repeats are logged at DEBUG only.
- Reopen 1.0 s later.
- 'ERROR: esp32c5-ttyACM2: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2 opened)' at 15.26 s after connect.
- Reconnect 5.03 s later; the cycle is about 20.3 s.

The hopper sends CHANNELS every 200 ms even while the board is silent.

Kismet shows 'Kismet external interface shutting down: ...' and error 'remote connection triggered shutdown: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2 opened)'.

For comparison, a C local source logs 'esp32c5-ttyACM2: no answer, reconnecting' at +6.0 s and 'IPC connection closed' at +15.1 s. Kismet re-opens after 5 s, and once logged a doubled re-open counted as an extra failure.
answers.evidence:
Other Troubleshooting rows (p8.out, p8b.out, p5, p4):
- Normal start: 'connected, offering it to Kismet as <UUID>' / 'opening <port> for <radio>' / '<port> opened' / '<port> capturing'.
- Kismet SIGSTOP for 20 s: 'connection ended: no PING from Kismet for 15 s', 11.9 s after the STOP. After SIGCONT, Kismet dropped the first reconnect ('did not get a ping response from the capture', 'Error reconnecting ... - source closed'); the next one captured.
- close_source.cmd gives 'connection ended: Connection to remote host was lost.', NOT the table's 'Kismet shut the source down: <reason>'.
- Missing port: '/dev/ttyACM9 is not there; is the board plugged in? (waiting for it)'.
- Bad hop list: 'Removed 2 channels ...'.

The board was recovered with esptool chip-id (hard reset) and answered START with link type 127.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: The wiki says sibling 1.0.0 captures Wi-Fi, but on this hardware it delivers no Wi-Fi records at all
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: On D8:0C, 1.0.0 answered START with link type 127, then sent 0 records: 0 packets in 40 s with a C local hopping source (which still logged 'capturing (wifi)'), and 0 bytes raw after CHANNELS 6, CHANNEL 6, CHANNELS 1-13 and 1,6,11, before and after an esptool hard reset. On the same board, 1.1.0 gave 613 packets and 1.2.0 gave 792. Cause not isolated; the 1.0.0 source's capture path matches 1.1.0.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Change the 1.0.0 row and sentences to: answers START but streamed no Wi-Fi frames on the test boards (ESP32-C5 rev v1.0); flash this project's image. Mark 1.1.0 as tested: Wi-Fi and Zigbee work, BTLE fails.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: FAQ and Firmware-Protocol text about the sibling firmware is now out of date
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: FAQ.md:80-82 says no board on 1.2.0 has run under Kismet and two of four did not answer START. D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image answered START first time in every test and captured all three radios under all three helper setups. Firmware-Protocol.md:444 says 1.1.0 'refuses' MODE BLE, but it silently ignores it (no reply, no reboot, the stream stays link type 127).
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Mark the 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 rows as tested on a real board (2026-09-29) and keep the non-answering-boards note as an unexplained earlier observation. Change 'refused' to 'ignored'. Resolve these VERIFY markers: Bluetooth-LE-Capture.md:32, 43, 57, 82, 87, 90 and Guide-BLE-Advertising-Survey.md:32, 50, 65, 81, 101.

code_corrections.problem: Line 34: both helpers take only an exclusive flock.
code_corrections.correct: Both also set TIOCEXCL on the tty (Linux, not ptys). A host program that opens the port while a helper has it gets EBUSY unless it has CAP_SYS_ADMIN, whether or not it takes the flock.

code_corrections.problem: 'One program at a time' names only flock as the lock a host should take.
code_corrections.correct: Both helpers take the flock and then set TIOCEXCL on a real tty (not a pty). A host of your own should treat EBUSY on open as 'in use', and should end the mode with TIOCNXCL before closing.

code_corrections.problem: Lines 422 and 424 document the old UART log wording: 'MODE needs WIFI or 802154' (noting that BLE is accepted too), and 'restarting to capture with the ... radio', which 'also says Wi-Fi when switching to Bluetooth LE'.
code_corrections.correct: Line 422: `MODE needs WIFI, 802154 or BLE`, for MODE without an argument. Line 424: `restarting to capture with the 802.15.4 radio` (or `Bluetooth LE`, `Wi-Fi`), for MODE to another radio. The 'says Wi-Fi when switching to Bluetooth LE' note goes; the old wording remains only on boards flashed with a build from before this fix.
